SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists: A Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Multi-Task Learning for LLMs

分类方向推理、智能体与后训练 / 后训练与对齐主题reinforcement learning
Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Shangqing Tu, Hongbang Yuan, Yushi Bai, Kang Liu et al.
high · 2026-08-06

为什么值得看 这项工作直接解释了多任务后训练中监督微调为何互相冲突、强化学习为何更易共存：它把差异归因于更新的稀疏性、近似正交性以及优势归一化和在线优化带来的低方差约束，并据此支持并行强化学习以提升多任务训练效率和灵活性。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 32）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

论文研究大语言模型多任务推理训练中监督微调的任务冲突及强化学习的稳定共存现象。

02
方法

论文结合参数层面的更新分析与多任务梯度干扰理论，比较两种训练方式的干扰边界。

03
差异

并行强化学习将多任务训练解耦，并利用强化学习更新的低方差和近似正交性质。

04
证据

实验观察到强化学习产生稀疏、近似正交的跨任务更新，理论结果则给出监督微调和强化学习不同的干扰约束。

摘要

监督微调和强化学习在提升大语言模型的多任务推理能力时表现出根本差异：监督微调在多阶段训练中产生严重任务冲突，而强化学习能让多种任务稳定共存。经验分析显示，强化学习在不同任务间产生稀疏且近似正交的参数更新；理论分析进一步指出，监督微调中的干扰受梯度绝对大小限制，而强化学习中的干扰受优势归一化和在线优化诱导的梯度方差限制，因此优化方向接近正交。基于这一发现，论文提出并行强化学习，以解耦多任务训练并提升效率与灵活性。

为什么值得看 这项工作针对音频推理强化学习中的奖励错配：结果奖励可能让模型忽略音频，固定过程奖励又难以适应不同问题和不断提升的策略。若其自演化、以声学证据为依据的评分确实带来三个基准上的显著提升，它为训练既关注声音内容又进行多步推理的模型提供了比静态规则更灵活的后训练信号。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 9）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有结果奖励只检查最终答案，而过程奖励依赖粗糙、手工设计且固定的标准。

02
方法

方法从原始波形合成逐样本量规，并依据模型轨迹按组更新和重加权评分标准。

03
差异

奖励同时扎根于声学证据，并随当前策略的薄弱点和问题需求变化。

04
证据

论文报告其在三个音频推理基准上显著超过多种开源和训练型基线，并改善音频感知。

摘要

音频推理对于机器理解声学世界至关重要，但仅监督最终答案可能使模型不关注音频，固定且粗糙的过程标准又难以适应不同问题和策略变化。本文介绍音频量规强化学习框架，根据原始波形为每个样本生成量规，并结合模型自身的轨迹按组重新生成和加权标准，从而提供持续、细粒度且扎根于音频证据的奖励信号；在三个音频推理基准上的评测显示，该方法显著优于多种基线，其收益随量规生成器和评判器能力提升而增加，并能收敛到稳定的推理长度。

为什么值得看 这项工作把情绪感知、理解和交互统一到一个多模态模型中，并用多任务强化学习协调奖励分配；对研究情感推理和后训练的读者，它提供了从专用任务模型转向统一模型的具体数据与优化方案。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有情感多模态研究主要按任务分别训练，任务协同和潜在推理能力没有得到充分利用。

02
方法

方法先用人工参与流程构建包含显式推理轨迹的情感世界数据集，再结合统一多任务奖励分配进行强化学习。

03
差异

情感和弦通过统一奖励协调多个情感任务，而不是为每个任务单独进行优化。

04
证据

论文报告称，模型在多数基准上超过同规模基线，并以更少参数取得接近商业模型的效果。

摘要

多模态大语言模型已展现出较强的情感智能，但现有研究多集中于任务专门化，忽视任务间协同，也未充分挖掘潜在推理能力。作者构建了包含十三万条数据的情感世界数据集，通过人工参与的流程将情感知识提炼为显式推理轨迹，并在此基础上进行监督微调；随后提出情感和弦强化学习策略，以统一的多任务奖励分配稳定优化，从而得到能够处理情绪感知、理解和交互的统一情感模型。大量实验表明，该模型在多数基准上超过同规模基线，且参数量显著少于商业模型时仍取得有竞争力的结果。

high · 2026-08-08

为什么值得看 它把视觉语言模型后训练的奖励信号从“答对即可”推进到“答对且依赖正确局部证据”，为减少语言先验、数据集捷径和无关视觉信息带来的幻觉提供了直接训练机制；对关注视觉 grounding 与可验证推理的研究者尤其有价值。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 3）
方法解读
01
问题

现有后训练方法不能检验答案是否因果依赖支持它的局部图像证据。

02
方法

方法中和对象级证据区域，并将相对于匹配非证据区域的支持度下降与答案正确性一起用于群体相对策略优化奖励。

03
差异

它使用弱对象级候选区域替代问题特定证据标注，同时在训练时进行证据审计且不增加推理开销。

04
证据

论文报告该方法在九个公开基准和四个骨干模型上超过此前基于强化学习的后训练方法，并通过定向分析验证对象级信号。

摘要

视觉语言模型应依据图像中的具体证据作答，而不是依赖语言先验、数据集捷径或无关视觉上下文。现有感知感知型后训练方法通过全局扰动或注意力代理鼓励模型使用图像，却无法检验生成答案是否因果依赖支持该答案的局部证据。本文提出反事实证据解耦，将证据区域中和后答案支持度的下降与匹配的非证据区域进行比较，并把这一信号与答案正确性结合到群体相对策略优化中，从而奖励依赖证据路径而非捷径或干扰路径的正确答案；该方法使用弱对象级候选区域，无需问题特定的证据标注，也不增加推理时开销。在九个公开基准和四个骨干模型上，该方法优于此前基于强化学习的后训练方法，针对性分析也验证了其面向对象的证据信号。

为什么值得看 该方法把视频生成从推理路径移到训练阶段，使自动驾驶规划器直接预测轨迹，同时保留视频动态先验；这为需要低延迟部署的端到端驾驶系统提供了比在线未来帧生成更简单的方案，并支持用强化学习优化超越轨迹模仿的组合驾驶奖励。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 22）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有世界动作模型在推理时生成未来视频，带来较高的计算延迟。

02
方法

方法通过联合流匹配协同训练视频专家与动作专家，并用隔离注意力掩码阻断动作分支对未来帧的依赖。

03
差异

视频专家与动作专家不共享参数，只通过统一注意力接口交互，因此训练后可丢弃视频分支并独立替换或扩展两类专家。

04
证据

该方法在导航仿真基准上报告百分之九十一点五的驾驶性能分数、较低延迟、超过现有世界动作模型规划器，并零样本迁移到大规模驾驶数据集。

摘要

世界动作模型能够通过把视频动态先验迁移到动作预测中提升端到端自动驾驶性能，但现有方法在推理时需要昂贵的未来视频生成。该研究让视频生成只作为训练信号，通过联合流匹配共同训练预训练视频专家和轻量动作专家，并利用隔离注意力掩码使动作预测不依赖未来帧；训练后可移除视频分支，仅保留直接预测轨迹的规划器。该方法在导航仿真基准上取得百分之九十一点五的驾驶性能分数，以显著更低的延迟超过现有世界动作模型规划器，并能零样本迁移到大规模真实驾驶数据集。

Kuo-Chung Peng, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chen-Yu Liu, En-Jui Kuo, Yun-Yuan Wang et al.
medium · 2026-07-30

为什么值得看 这项工作把快速权重序列模型的统一记忆门控改为逐坐标控制，适合需要长上下文且快状态各维度具有不同记忆时间尺度的量子或量子启发式预测任务；在量子启发模块参与快速编程器的架构中，互补矩阵门控相较标量门控将多步预测误差至少降低了百分之九十一点二。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 2）
方法解读
01
问题

标量门控让所有快速状态坐标共享同一个保留与写入比例及记忆时间尺度。

02
方法

方法用低秩生成的逐元素调制控制新候选分支、旧状态分支或两者，并用互补矩阵门控分别保留旧状态和写入新候选。

03
差异

互补矩阵门控在保留有界凸更新与仿射前缀扫描的同时，把统一门扩展为坐标级记忆控制。

04
证据

作者在四类快速权重编程器、七个单步预测基准和五种序列长度上比较方法，并报告量子启发式架构中最稳定的收益。

摘要

序列模型需要决定向记忆中写入什么以及保留什么；在量子和量子启发式序列学习中，非线性循环更新通常需要反复执行电路并进行跨时间反向传播，使长上下文代价高昂。本文提出自调制量子启发式科洛莫戈罗夫—阿诺德网络快速权重编程器，并进一步提出互补矩阵门控：用一个逐元素矩阵门保留旧状态，用其互补量写入新候选状态，从而在保持有界凸更新和仿射前缀扫描结构的同时实现坐标级记忆控制；在七个单步预测基准和五种序列长度上，互补矩阵门控对包含量子启发式快速模块的架构带来最稳定的改进，在杰恩斯—卡明斯和超导量子比特—谐振器动力学的直接多步预测中，各预测跨度的均方误差维持在约千分之一或更低，并较标量门控至少改善百分之九十一点二。

high · 2026-08-07

为什么值得看 这项工作把深伪视频检测从单一模型判断转为纹理、光照、运动和物理四个视角的协同取证，并用裁判智能体整合证据；如果其跨域结果可复现，它为应对新型生成器和细微伪造痕迹提供了比单模型或单一分析视角更稳健的路线，尤其适合关注安全检测泛化的研究者。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 3）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有深伪检测基准难以覆盖新型生成方法，单模型检测器也难以捕捉细微伪造痕迹并跨域泛化。

02
方法

数据集通过多模型聚合与冲突消解生成细粒度观察标注，检测器由四个领域专家智能体和一个裁判智能体组成。

03
差异

系统将取证分析拆分为纹理、光照、运动和物理四种独立视角，而不是依赖单一模型或单一证据来源。

04
证据

在域外测试中，完全由小型开源多模态大语言模型构成的系统超过闭源模型，并在该基准所有报告指标上排名第一。

摘要

生成式人工智能被滥用于制作高度逼真的深伪视频，带来伦理和人工智能安全风险，但现有基准对近期合成方法覆盖不足，也缺少可靠的细粒度文本标注。本文构建了包含十万个视频、覆盖三十三种合成方法的深伪视频数据集，并通过四个专长智能体分别分析纹理、光照、运动和物理线索，再由裁判智能体汇总预测与解释；在域外测试中，该框架完全由小型开源多模态大语言模型组成，却超过包括闭源模型在内的所有对比方法，并在该基准的全部报告指标上排名第一。

为什么值得看 这篇综述把五类视觉内容保护方法放到同一生命周期和评估框架下，指出多数方法仍只对静态或弱自适应攻击者有效；对研究鲁棒性、数据保护和多模态智能体的读者，它提供了比较迁移性、适应性与部署成熟度的入口，也明确了从受控基准走向真实对手的缺口。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 3）
方法解读
01
问题

视觉资产在发布、训练、编辑、访问和流通后可能被未经授权地识别、训练、仿制、自动化获取或使用。

02
方法

综述按视觉资产生命周期归纳五类保护方法，并用可迁移性、适应性和部署准备度进行横向评估。

03
差异

它将原本分属不同研究社区、成功标准不兼容的防护技术统一为所有者侧的主动干预问题。

04
证据

作者报告各类方法大多只在静态或弱自适应对手和受控基准上得到验证。

摘要

视觉内容进入人工智能流程后，所有者通常难以继续控制其使用方式，因此技术保护往往需要在内容发布或访问时提前介入。本综述将这一保护范式称为“为善而生的对抗攻击”，考察隐私过滤器、不可学习样本、生成式防护、对抗性验证码和来源追踪机制五类方法，并从可迁移性、适应性和部署准备度等共同维度进行比较；综述发现，大多数保护仍主要在静态或弱自适应对手上验证，受控基准之外的证据十分有限。

方法解读
01
问题

在开放手脚架上收集的微调轨迹会使模型依赖训练手脚架的规划约定。

SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists: A Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Multi-Task Learning for LLMs

CategoryAreaReasoning, Agents, and Post-Training / Post-Training and AlignmentTopicreinforcement learning
Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Shangqing Tu, Hongbang Yuan, Yushi Bai, Kang Liu et al.
high · 2026-08-06

Why it matters This paper gives a concrete explanation for why multi-task SFT can interfere while RL tasks coexist: sparse, near-orthogonal RL updates and the variance control from advantage normalization and on-policy optimization may make concurrent task training more stable, motivating Parallel-RL for better efficiency and flexibility.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 32)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper studies task conflicts in multi-stage SFT and stable task coexistence under multi-task RL for LLM reasoning.

02
Method

It combines parameter-level update analysis with a theoretical analysis of multi-task gradient interference.

03
Difference

Parallel-RL decouples multi-task training while exploiting the low-variance, approximately orthogonal update structure attributed to RL.

04
Evidence

Experiments observe sparse and approximately orthogonal cross-task RL updates, while the theory derives norm-limited SFT interference and variance-limited RL interference.

Abstract

Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) exhibit fundamentally different behaviors in enhancing multi-task reasoning for large language models (LLMs). Our preliminary experiments revealed a phenomenon: SFT suffers from severe task conflicts under multi-stage training, whereas RL enables stable coexistence across diverse tasks. Empirically, we trace this to the parameter level, observing that RL induces sparse and approximately orthogonal updates across tasks. We provide a theoretical explanation for this mechanism by analyzing multi-task gradient interference. Our results reveal a distinction: interference in SFT is norm-limited, scaling with the absolute gradient magnitude, whereas interference in RL is variance-limited, bounded by the gradient variance induced by advantage normalization and on-policy optimization. This small variance bound yields near-orthogonal optimization directions across tasks. Leveraging this insight, we propose Parallel-RL, a paradigm that decouples multi-task training, significantly improving efficiency and flexibility.

Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning

CategoryAreaReasoning, Agents, and Post-Training / Post-Training and AlignmentTopicreinforcement learning
Fangxu Yu, Tao Feng, Dehai Min, Zinan Lin, Weijia Xu, Michael Xu et al.
high · 2026-08-03

Why it matters This work addresses reward misalignment in audio-reasoning RL: outcome rewards can let a model ignore the audio, while fixed process rewards do not adapt to question demands or policy improvement. If the reported gains across three benchmarks hold, audio-grounded evolving rubrics offer a more targeted post-training signal for models that must combine acoustic perception with multi-step reasoning.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 9)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Outcome rewards supervise only the final answer, while process rewards use coarse, hand-crafted, and static criteria.

02
Method

The framework generates per-sample rubrics from raw waveforms and updates and reweights them from grouped model rollouts.

03
Difference

04
Evidence

The paper reports substantial gains over open-source and training-based baselines on three audio-reasoning benchmarks, along with improved audio perception.

Abstract

Audio reasoning is essential for machine understanding of the acoustic world. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can elicit such reasoning, yet existing reward designs are complementary in their limitations: outcome-based rewards supervise only the final answer and let the model reach it without attending to the audio, whereas process-based rewards score the reasoning itself but rely on coarse, hand-crafted, and fixed criteria that neither adapt to each question nor stay grounded in the acoustic evidence. Moreover, questions differ in what they demand, with some hinging on perception and others on multi-step reasoning, and any static criterion weakens as the policy improves. Supervising the reasoning process with fine-grained, audio-grounded, and adaptive rewards is therefore crucial, yet challenging since such rewards are impractical to design by hand for every sample. To this end, we introduce AudioRubrics, a reinforcement learning framework that supervises audio reasoning with self-evolving, audio-grounded rubric rewards. AudioRubrics synthesizes per-sample rubrics from the raw waveform and, conditioned on the model's own rollouts, regenerates and reweights criteria per group, supplying a continuous learning signal that keeps targeting the current policy's weaknesses as static criteria saturate. Comprehensive evaluations across three audio reasoning benchmarks reveal that AudioRubrics substantially outperforms a wide range of open-source and training-based baselines. Furthermore, our analysis shows that the gains scale with the capability of the rubric generator and judge, and AudioRubrics converges to a stable reasoning length that avoids both degenerate collapse and unbounded growth. The improvement in audio perception further demonstrates the effectiveness of anchoring supervision in the acoustic evidence. Our project page is available at https://audiorubrics.github.io.

Method brief

Abstract

Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in emotional intelligence. However, prevailing research predominantly focuses on task-specific specialization, often neglecting inter-task synergy and leaving latent reasoning potential underexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce OneEmo, a unified affective generalist capable of mastering emotion perception, comprehension, and interaction. For this purpose, we first construct EmoWorld-130K, a comprehensive dataset that distills specialized affective knowledge into explicit reasoning trajectories via a human-in-the-loop workflow. Supervised fine-tuning on this corpus reveals significant mutual benefits derived from multi-task learning. Second, to fully unlock the latent reasoning potential, we propose Emo-Chord, a novel reinforcement learning strategy that stabilizes optimization through unified multi-task reward allocation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OneEmo achieves state-of-the-art performance against similarly sized baselines across most benchmarks. Notably, despite having significantly fewer parameters than commercial models, OneEmo delivers highly competitive results. This paper paves the way for more reliable and interpretable affective computing. The code is available at https://github.com/waHAHJIAHAO/OneEmo.

Method brief
01
Problem

Existing perception-aware post-training does not test whether an answer causally depends on the local image evidence that supports it.

02
Method

CED neutralizes an object-centric evidence region, compares the support drop with matched non-evidence regions, and combines this signal with answer correctness in GRPO.

Abstract

Vision-Language Models (VLMs) should answer from concrete image evidence rather than language priors, dataset shortcuts, or irrelevant visual context. Existing perception-aware post-training methods encourage image use through global perturbations or attention proxies, but they do not test whether a sampled answer causally depends on the local evidence that supports it. We propose Counterfactual Evidence Disentanglement (CED), a training-time evidence audit for VLM grounding. For each response, CED neutralizes an object-centric Evidence Region and compares the resulting support drop against matched non-evidence Regions. We combine this signal with answer correctness inside GRPO, rewarding correct answers that rely on the evidence path rather than shortcut or nuisance paths. CED uses weak object-level proposals, requires no question-specific evidence annotations, and adds no inference-time overhead. Across nine public benchmarks and four backbones, CED outperforms prior RL-based post-training methods, with targeted analyses verifying its object-centric signal.

SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

Zongchuang Zhao, Xin Zhou, Tianyang Xu, Zhengyang Sun, Kaixuan Zhou, Honglin Li et al.
high · 2026-08-07

Why it matters For autonomous-driving algorithm researchers, SimWAM shows that video generation can supply a dynamics prior during training without remaining in the inference loop. This directly targets the latency cost of future-frame generation, while reinforcement learning extends the planner beyond trajectory imitation; the design is most useful for low-latency planners that still want to benefit from advances in video models.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 22)
Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing world-action models incur expensive inference because they generate future video frames.

02
Method

SimWAM jointly trains a pretrained video expert and a lightweight action expert with flow matching, while an isolated attention mask prevents action prediction from using future frames.

03
Difference

The experts share no parameters and communicate only through a unified attention interface, so the video branch can be removed after training and the two experts can be scaled independently.

04
Evidence

The paper reports 91.5 PDMS on NAVSIM, lower latency than existing WAM-based planners, and zero-shot transfer to nuScenes, with reinforcement learning used for a compositional driving reward.

Abstract

World-Action Models (WAMs) improve end-to-end autonomous driving by transferring video dynamics priors to action prediction, but existing methods require costly future generation at inference. We present SimWAM, a simple yet effective WAM that uses video generation purely as a training signal. It co-trains a pretrained video expert and a lightweight action expert with joint flow matching. An isolated attention mask keeps action prediction independent of future frames, allowing the video branch to be discarded after training and leaving a self-contained planner that directly predicts trajectories. Since the two experts share no parameters and interact only through a unified attention interface, the video backbone could be replaced and the action expert scaled independently without modifying the learning objective or inference pipeline. We further apply reinforcement learning to optimize a compositional driving reward beyond trajectory imitation. Our SimWAM achieves 91.5 PDMS on NAVSIM, surpasses state-of-the-art WAM-based planners with substantially lower latency, and transfers zero-shot to nuScenes. These results position SimWAM as a simple yet solid baseline that could readily benefit from advances in video generation for efficient autonomous driving. The code and model weights are available at https://github.com/H-EmbodVis/SimWAM/

Complementary Matrix-Gated QKAN Fast-Weight Programmers for Quantum Dynamics Forecasting

Kuo-Chung Peng, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chen-Yu Liu, En-Jui Kuo, Yun-Yuan Wang et al.
medium · 2026-07-30

Why it matters This work gives fast-weight sequence models coordinate-wise memory control instead of forcing every fast-state dimension to share one timescale. For quantum or quantum-inspired forecasting, CMG preserves the efficient convex prefix-scan update and improves direct multi-step forecasts over scalar-gated counterparts by at least 91.2%.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 2)
Method brief
01
Problem

Scalar gating forces all fast-state coordinates to use the same retention-write balance and memory timescale.

02
Method

The paper applies low-rank element-wise modulation to the proposal branch, the old-state branch, or both, and uses one sigmoid matrix gate with its complement for retention and writing.

03
Difference

Complementary Matrix Gating adds coordinate-wise memory control while retaining the bounded convex update and affine prefix-scan structure of scalar gating.

04
Evidence

The study compares four modulation rules across four fast-weight programmer architectures, seven single-step benchmarks, and five sequence lengths, with additional Jaynes-Cummings and transmon-resonator forecasting tests.

Abstract

Sequence models must decide what to write into memory and what to retain. In quantum and quantum-inspired sequence learning, nonlinear recurrent updates often require repeated circuit evaluations and sequential backpropagation through time, making long contexts costly. Gated fast-weight programmers (FWPs) based on quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (QKANs) alleviate this bottleneck by storing context in time-varying fast parameters. However, their scalar gate applies one retention-write balance to every fast-state coordinate, forcing all parameters to share a memory timescale. We introduce Self-Modulating QKAN-based FWPs, which replace this broadcast gate with low-rank-generated element-wise modulation of the new-proposal branch, a bounded old-state branch, or both. We further propose Complementary Matrix Gating (CMG), which uses one sigmoid matrix gate to retain the old state and its complement to write the new proposal. CMG provides coordinate-wise memory control while preserving the bounded convex update and affine prefix-scan structure of scalar gating, at the modulation-head cost of a single-branch rule. We compare four self-modulating rules with scalar gating across four FWP architectures combining classical and QKAN-based slow and fast programmers. Across seven single-step forecasting benchmarks and five sequence lengths, CMG gives the most consistent improvements for architectures whose fast programmer incorporates a QKAN-based module. In direct multi-step forecasting of Jaynes-Cummings and transmon-resonator dynamics simulated with CUDA-Q Dynamics, CMG models maintain mean-squared errors on the order of 0.001 or lower across forecasting horizons of 4, 8, and 16 steps, while improving on their scalar-gated counterparts by at least 91.2%. These results establish coordinate-wise complementary modulation as a stable and effective update for QKAN-based FWPs.

Code
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing benchmarks underrepresent recent synthesis methods, while single-model detectors often miss subtle artifacts and generalize poorly to emerging generators.

02
Method

Abstract

The malicious use of generative artificial intelligence to create highly realistic deepfake videos raises serious ethical concerns and poses substantial challenges to AI safety. However, existing deepfake video benchmarks provide limited coverage of recent synthesis methods and generally lack reliable fine-grained textual annotations. Meanwhile, conventional detectors and multimodal large language models (MLLMs), whether operating as a single model or relying on a single analytical perspective, often fail to capture subtle forgery artifacts, limiting their generalization to emerging AI-generated methods. To address these limitations, we introduce FaceVid-Forensics-100K, a large-scale deepfake video dataset comprising 100,000 videos and spanning 33 synthesis methods across face swapping, face reenactment, and entire-face synthesis, including recent generators such as Seedance 2.0. The dataset provides fine-grained textual annotations of visual observations and verdict-consistent forensic explanations, automatically synthesized through a multi-model aggregation and conflict-resolution pipeline powered by advanced MLLMs. Building on this benchmark, we propose a multi-agent forensic reasoning framework that employs four specialized domain-expert agents to independently analyze forgery cues from four perspectives: texture, lighting, motion, and physics. A judge agent then reconciles their reports to produce a final prediction together with an explanation. Extensive evaluations on out-of-domain test sets show that, despite being composed entirely of small open-source MLLMs, our framework outperforms all methods including closed-source GPT and Gemini models and ranks first across all reported metrics on this benchmark. 01

Abstract

Once visual content enters an AI pipeline, its owner often retains little technical control over how it is used. Legal and regulatory remedies can address misuse, but many technical interventions must be applied earlier, when content is released or accessed. This survey examines the protective paradigm that has grown around this intervention point, which we call adversarial attacks for good. Perturbations and structured signals long studied as attacks on learned models are instead applied by data owners, creators, platforms, or auditors to disrupt unauthorized automation or support later accountability. Five research communities have arrived at this inversion largely independently, each addressing a different stage of a visual asset's lifecycle: privacy filters against unwanted recognition at sharing time, unlearnable examples against unauthorized training, generative safeguards against malicious editing or imitation, adversarial CAPTCHAs for access control against automated agents, and provenance mechanisms for post-circulation attribution. Although developed in separate venues with incompatible success criteria, many of these methods exploit persistent gaps between human perception, semantic interpretation, and machine inference, suggesting that the paradigm remains relevant as visual pipelines evolve toward multimodal models and autonomous agents. To make their claims comparable, we evaluate all five families along shared axes of transferability, adaptability, and deployment readiness. Across the lifecycle, we find that most protections are still validated mainly against static or weakly adaptive adversaries, while evidence beyond controlled benchmarks remains scarce. We close by consolidating cross-stage countermeasures and open problems for robust, composable, and deployable owner-side protection.

Method brief

Problem

Method

Abstract

CLI-based software-engineering agents have matured rapidly, yet the open ecosystem has converged on a single training environment: trajectory datasets used to fine-tune open models are collected almost exclusively under OpenHands. Models fine-tuned on this data score well under OpenHands but degrade substantially when deployed under any non-training scaffold. Untrained base models do not show this divergence, indicating the gap is fine-tuning-induced and tied to the conventions of the training scaffold. We argue that a load-bearing scaffold-specific behavior is planning structure, in two senses this paper distinguishes: explicit planning, a pre-execution plan produced as a first-class artifact, and implicit planning, the structural conventions that shape execution throughout the agent loop. Under this hypothesis, closing the gap requires moving planning from a fixed scaffold artifact to a learned model capability. We introduce Decoupling CLI Agent Scaffolding (DCAS), a backend-substitution interception layer that routes API traffic between any CLI scaffold and any backend model without modifying the scaffold, enabling cross-scaffold evaluation and planning-aware trajectory collection. Using DCAS, a controlled plan-source intervention confirms planning quality is a high-leverage component, with gains exceeding the cross-scaffold drops we observe. A model fine-tuned on a small set of DCAS-collected planning-aware trajectories under a single scaffold gains consistently across non-training scaffolds, and the two senses of planning are empirically separable in training data.

Abstract

Deploying autonomous multimodal agents in continuous, real-world environments requires them to ingest unbounded audio-visual streams and maintain hour-scale memory. However, current evaluations predominantly rely on brief clips and multiple-choice formats. This design allows minimal baselines that process only the last four frames to match or surpass complex streaming models, while answer options also expose language shortcuts. We introduce StreamArena, a benchmark for hour-scale, interactive streaming video understanding. StreamArena contains 243 full-length videos averaging 88.8 minutes and 3,646 rigorously annotated, open-ended question-answer pairs that evaluate real-time perception, historical retrospection, proactive interaction, and multimodal tool utilization. Evaluation across diverse systems exposes a tension between continuous interaction and long-horizon multimodal comprehension. Methods that retain only recent frames cannot recover distant events, methods that convert past observations into text lose visual evidence, and methods that repeatedly compress visual memory struggle to preserve fine-grained details over time. We address this tension with StreamMind, a two-tier architecture that assigns latency-critical interaction and proactive monitoring to independently scheduled frontend workers, while backend workers asynchronously construct persistent multimodal memory and perform historical recall and external search. StreamMind outperforms existing streaming baselines across all four capabilities and reduces query-to-answer latency by reusing persistent state.

Method brief
01
Problem

02

Generic parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods transferred from language models can fail silently on real-time detectors, whose heterogeneous operators and detection-specific components impose placement constraints absent from regular Transformer stacks. We propose YOLO-PEFT, a structure-aware framework that formulates adapter placement as an auditable constraint-planning problem. Given a detector graph, a PEFT request, and a resource budget, YOLO-PEFT assigns operator and semantic roles, evaluates explicit operator-validity, detector-semantic, graph-interface, and deployment predicates, records a reason code for each excluded module, and either emits a budgeted target-module plan or returns Refuse before training. On RT-DETR-L, all seven evaluated LoRA-family configurations cross the predefined catastrophic threshold, supporting a calibrated Refuse-to-Full-SFT decision within the evaluated coverage. A controlled YOLO11 audit further shows that LoRA reduces peak training memory by 43.9 percent, although training takes 1.72 times longer. Within the evaluated detector families, placement policies, and calibration coverage, YOLO-PEFT replaces manual target-module trial and error with explicit, inspectable planning while preserving verified train-save-merge-export paths; refusal on unseen detector architectures remains an open validation problem. Method brief
01

Abstract

We further quantify the protocol's internal reliability through inter-judge agreement and bootstrap ranking stability. We release standardized evaluation scripts, model outputs, and aggregation tools at https://github.com/Multimodal-Intelligence-Lab/CLIP-CC-Bench to support reproducibility. CLIP-CC-Bench provides a practical evaluation framework for long-form video description, filling a gap left by existing short-clip and QA-only benchmarks.

high · 2026-08-03

Why it matters DME addresses the practical trade-off between fast but coarse contrastive embeddings and discriminative but costly chain-of-thought generation by moving latent reasoning and cross-direction reconstruction into training, while retaining standard contrastive-encoder serving cost. This is directly useful for search, recommendation, and agent systems that must support billion-scale indexes and fine-grained multimodal matching.

Source signalsHugging Face Daily Papers (community upvotes 👍 8)
Method brief
01
Problem

Existing multimodal embedding models struggle to combine billion-scale indexing efficiency with fine-grained discrimination on hard matches.

02
Method

The model performs large-scale contrastive pre-training followed by training-time Evidence-Grounded Typed Latent Reasoning and Cross-Conditional Reconstruction.

03
Difference

The auxiliary mechanisms operate only during training and replace online explicit generation with hidden-space reasoning and cross-directional autoregressive reconstruction.

04
Evidence

The reported two-billion and nine-billion variants score 74.8 and 78.4 on MMEB-v2, while production evaluation reports a 2.92% relative offline gain and a 0.1% online search lift.

Abstract

Multimodal representation learning is a cornerstone of modern AI. By encoding multimodal queries and targets into vectors, it powers industrial search and recommendation and underpins modern agents. Real-world platforms with complex modalities and massive-scale content, such as Douyin, Xiaohongshu, and YouTube, demand both efficiency under billion-scale indexing and fine-grained discrimination for hard matching. Existing MLLM embedding models rarely satisfy both. Contrastive models are efficient but rely on pair-level supervision too coarse for fine-grained distinctions, while CoT-based models improve discrimination through explicit generation impractical to serve online. We present Douyin Multimodal Embedding (DME), a model trained in two stages to combine both strengths. Stage 1 performs large-scale contrastive pre-training that establishes a unified multimodal embedding space with broad modality and task coverage. Stage 2 supplements semantic sufficiency, the property that an embedding is grounded in retrieval-relevant evidence and preserves fine-grained counterpart-side semantics, via two mechanisms. Evidence-Grounded Typed Latent Reasoning organizes retrieval evidence through hidden-space latent reasoning, and Cross-Conditional Reconstruction enforces counterpart-side semantics through cross-directional autoregressive reconstruction. Both act only during training and add only marginal query-side overhead, so DME serves as efficiently as a standard contrastive encoder. On MMEB-v2, DME reaches state-of-the-art results at comparable scales for its 2B and 9B variants (74.8 and 78.4), with especially strong video and visual-document tasks. In production, DME delivers a 2.92% relative gain on Douyin's in-house offline evaluation set, is deployed across Douyin scenarios such as generative, image, and AI search, and yields a 0.1% Lifetime (LT) gain in online A/B testing on Douyin search.

UnionSparse: An Index-Efficient Sparsity Framework for Low-Bit Sparse LLM Inference on Edge

分类方向编译器、内核与硬件 / GPU/加速器内核主题accelerator / edge inference
Tianhao Jiang, Hang Gu, Teng Wang, Qianyu Cheng, ZhenDong Zheng, Cheng Tang et al.
high · 2026-08-10

为什么值得看 这项工作指出，低比特稀疏推理的瓶颈不只是权重计算量，还包括稀疏索引流量和非零值提取；对需要在边缘 GPU 上运行小批量解码的系统，提升有效载荷与元数据比例可能比单纯压缩权重更关键。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

低比特量化减少了权重载荷，却没有按比例减少稀疏索引元数据，导致索引流量和非零值提取限制稀疏矩阵乘法。

02
方法

框架结合索引高效位图编码与低比特共享内存并行解码的稀疏矩阵乘法内核。

03
差异

位图编码摊薄元数据并让稀疏遍历配合片段组装，解码内核则针对小批量执行进行优化。

04
证据

在四比特权重四比特激活和百分之三十至百分之七十稀疏率下，论文报告相较多个稀疏、切分库及通用矩阵乘法库获得一点四三倍至三点四六倍加速。

摘要

边缘大语言模型推理同时采用稀疏化和低比特量化来满足设备的内存、延迟与功耗限制，但量化虽然缩小了权重载荷，却未同比减少稀疏元数据，使索引流量和非零值提取成为稀疏矩阵乘法的关键瓶颈。本文提出联合稀疏框架，通过索引高效位图编码摊薄元数据，并使用低比特共享内存并行解码改进小批量执行；在四比特权重四比特激活、百分之三十至百分之七十稀疏率下，框架相较于闪存大语言模型、稀疏推理器、切分库和通用矩阵乘法库取得了文中所报告的加速效果。

Measuring and Reducing WebGPU Dispatch Overhead for LLM Inference

分类方向编译器、内核与硬件 / GPU/加速器内核主题accelerator / edge inference
Jędrzej Maczan
high · 2026-08-09

为什么值得看 这项工作把浏览器端大语言模型推理的瓶颈从内核效率定位到操作分发次数：在批大小为一时，减少分发并摊薄分发成本可能比继续优化单个内核更有效，直接适用于网页和边缘设备推理引擎。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

浏览器端大语言模型推理中的网页图形处理接口分发开销缺少可靠测量，单操作测量还会混入同步成本。

02
方法

研究使用顺序分发测量方法，将连续分发产生的同步影响与单次分发成本区分开来。

03
差异

该方法不同于朴素的单操作基准，并把优化目标从内核质量转向分发次数。

04
证据

测量显示分发成本不随数据类型变化，批大小为一时分发开销而非内核质量成为瓶颈。

摘要

大语言模型已部署到浏览器和边缘设备等多种环境，网页图形处理接口作为跨平台标准得到广泛使用，但其每次操作分发的开销仍缺乏准确刻画。本文提出顺序分发测量方法，发现朴素的单操作测量会把同步开销混入分发开销；测量结果表明每次分发成本与数据类型无关，且在批大小为一时，推理瓶颈来自分发次数而非内核质量，因此应通过减少分发次数，并在推理引擎和网页图形处理接口规范中摊薄分发成本来优化浏览器端推理。

ReVolt: Power Delivery Network-Aware Voltage Droop Control for 2.5D PIM Chiplet Architectures

分类方向编译器、内核与硬件 / GPU/加速器内核主题accelerator / edge inference
Vibhanshu Sharma, Alish Kanani, Miao Sun, Janardhan Rao Doppa, Umit Y. Ogras, Partha Pratim Pande
medium · 2026-08-09

为什么值得看 这项工作把供电网络电压下陷纳入二维半导体封装存算一体系统的运行时控制，对需要在多芯粒平台上部署机器学习推理的硬件和系统研究者有直接价值：它用操作单元规模调节芯粒电流需求，在不牺牲推理精度的前提下避免电压违规，并相较固定和动态基线平均降低七十六倍能量延迟积。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

二维多芯粒存算一体系统中的空间和时间变化电流需求会触发供电网络电压下陷。

02
方法

框架使用长短期记忆网络代理模型预测各芯粒电压轨迹，并运行时调整操作单元规模。

03
差异

它把操作单元规模作为控制电流需求和供电电压下陷的主动控制旋钮，而不是采用固定或已有动态策略。

04
证据

实验显示该方法避免了电压下陷违规，相较现有基线平均降低七十六倍能量延迟积，且未损害推理精度。

摘要

基于存算一体的二维多芯粒平台适合机器学习负载，但芯粒电流需求的时空变化会引起供电网络电压下陷，造成电压违规、性能下降和推理精度受损。本文提出一种基于动态操作单元的控制框架，利用长短期记忆网络代理模型预测各芯粒的运行时供电电压轨迹，并主动调整操作单元规模以抑制下陷；实验表明，该方法可避免电压下陷违规，平均将能量延迟积降低七十六倍，同时保持机器学习模型的推理精度。

SpSYRK: Half the Work in Distributed Sparse Matrix Multiplication

Thomas McFarland, Julian Bellavita, Giulia Guidi
high · 2026-08-10

为什么值得看 这项工作把对称性直接下沉到分布式稀疏矩阵乘法的数据分块和通信中，适合相似度搜索、图分析和基因组数据处理；它既可替换现有的通用稀疏乘法实现，又能让后续操作直接消费三角形结果，从而减少计算、通信和内存开销。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

通用分布式稀疏矩阵乘法重复计算对称秩加一更新中不必要的工作。

02
方法

算法将输出非对角块分配到进程网格的上下三角区域，并在对角块中只计算下三角部分。

03
差异

第二个变体重新安排通信，因此无需显式生成输入矩阵的转置。

04
证据

在珀尔穆特三十二个节点上，局部乘法占主导时相对优化后的稀疏乘法获得两倍加速，并在高进程数下持续展现更好的扩展性。

摘要

对称秩加一更新计算矩阵与其转置的乘积，是机器学习、图分析和基因组学中相似度计算的基础，但现有分布式稀疏矩阵乘法通常把它当作通用乘法处理。本文利用输入和输出的对称性，只计算必要的输出区域，并通过重新安排通信来避免显式构造转置矩阵；在珀尔穆特超级计算机的三十二个节点上，相比优化后的稀疏乘法算法最高获得两倍加速，其优势取决于算术强度，并在高进程数下保持更好的扩展性。

论文 / 高优先级

PSP: Low-Overhead Packet-Level Load Balancing for Stale-State and Bandwidth-Asymmetric Networks

Jiaqi Liu, Chunyang Zhang, Heng Pan, Yanbiao Li
high · 2026-08-09

为什么值得看 这项工作直接针对人工智能数据中心中的微突发、多路径拥塞和异构链路负载均衡，适合关注训练网络或推理服务尾延迟的研究者。它用局部概率映射替代全局排序，在状态信息过时、链路带宽不一致和硬件资源受限时，声称能以较低硬件开销取得接近顶级候选选择方法的效果。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

流级哈希负载均衡无法及时感知链路状态，而现有分组级方法受过时状态、高硬件复杂度和异构链路适应性不足限制。

02
方法

算法将链路状态离散为区间，并依据状态映射分组被转发到各路径的概率。

03
差异

它用局部概率决策替代全局排序，以减少过时信息导致的羊群效应和振荡。

04
证据

周期精确模拟覆盖端口规模、带宽受限路径和固定流干扰，并报告了丢包率、缓冲区占用和可扩展性结果。

摘要

随着大型语言模型训练和生成式人工智能服务增长，数据中心网络面临严重的微突发流量与高并发，传统基于哈希的流级负载均衡无法感知链路状态，容易在多路径胖树网络中产生哈希碰撞、热点拥塞和尾延迟。本文提出概率状态比例分发算法，利用基于区间的离散状态表示和局部概率映射，降低硬件复杂度，并抑制过时状态引起的羊群效应与振荡；周期精确模拟表明，该方法在不同端口规模、带宽受限路径和固定流干扰下均较稳健，在丢包率、第九十九百分位缓冲区占用和可扩展性方面优于最短队列加入和随机调度，同时以更低硬件成本保持了与前几名候选选择方法相近的表现。

论文 / 重点关注

A Preliminary Study on Simultaneous Coscheduling for Discrete GPU vs. Fused GPU

Poorna Gunathilaka, Nabayan Chaudhury, Kirshanthan Sundararajah, Wu-chun Feng
medium · 2026-08-10

为什么值得看 这项研究直接关联异构系统运行时和内存管理：在GH200这类融合式CPU-GPU平台上，更多混合任务划分变得可行，托管内存也能在部分矩阵上实用，从而减少显式数据搬运的编程负担。对评估融合式加速器、协同调度策略和内存抽象的系统研究者尤其有参考价值，但证据目前局限于稀疏共轭梯度这一案例和初步实验。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

研究CPU-GPU协同执行的效率如何受到任务划分和内存架构影响。

02
方法

在GH200与H100PCIe上运行稀疏共轭梯度，并比较显式复制、托管内存和映射内存。

03
差异

研究将融合式与离散式GPU平台放在同一协同调度场景中，重点考察减少手动数据移动的代价。

04
证据

实验报告称GH200让多种混合任务划分具备竞争力，并使托管内存在部分矩阵上可用。

摘要

CPU-GPU协同调度允许应用同时使用两类处理器执行，但其效率取决于工作负载划分和内存架构。本文以稀疏共轭梯度为案例，在英伟达GH200超级芯片和离散式H100PCIe平台上，比较显式复制、托管内存和映射内存三种内存管理方式下的不同任务划分，并评估减少手动数据搬运所带来的运行时间与可编程性权衡。结果表明，相比H100PCIe，GH200使多种混合CPU-GPU任务划分具备竞争力，并使托管内存在若干矩阵上变得实用。

论文 / 高优先级

SwiftQK: Fast and Communication-Efficient Tensor Parallelism for Query-Key Normalization

分类方向编译器、内核与硬件 / GPU/加速器内核主题CUDA / kernel optimization
Gyudong Kim, Wonjun Han, Young Geun Kim
high · 2026-08-10

为什么值得看 这项工作直接降低张量并行大语言模型中查询与键归一化的通信开销，尤其适合受单步生成延迟限制的多卡推理服务；论文报告端到端每输出令牌时间平均降低百分之二十九点五，相比优化后的标量聚合实现仍降低百分之十四点三。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

张量并行的查询与键归一化需要跨卡获得完整隐藏向量，从而增加通信延迟。

02
方法

内核仅交换标量归一化统计量，并以持久化执行结合点到点归约和独立逐元素计算。

03
差异

它把标准的完整向量聚集改为标量统计交换，并在归约期间隐藏可并行的计算。

04
证据

归一化延迟相对标准实现降低百分之八十一点四至百分之九十三点九，端到端服务每输出令牌时间平均降低百分之二十九点五。

摘要

查询与键归一化能够改善现代大语言模型的训练稳定性和质量，但在张量并行下，其归一化因子依赖完整隐藏向量，会引入额外的跨卡通信。本文提出一种多卡均方根归一化内核，只交换标量归一化统计量，并在无死锁的持久化内核中，用独立的逐元素计算覆盖剩余的点到点归约；在近期大语言模型上的评测显示，相比使用完整向量聚集的标准张量并行实现，归一化延迟降低百分之八十一点四至百分之九十三点九，端到端服务的每输出令牌时间平均降低百分之二十九点五。

论文 / 高优先级

What Irregularity Costs: CUDA C++, Rust, and Triton on a Hash-Blocked GPU Workload

分类方向编译器、内核与硬件 / GPU/加速器内核主题CUDA / kernel optimization
Petr Korolev
high · 2026-08-08

为什么值得看 这项工作提醒内核和编译器工程师：在开放寻址、原子竞争和数据相关探测深度主导的图形处理器负载上，语言抽象会影响性能乃至正确性；它还定位了锈语言原子读取的缓存一致性代价，以及特里顿有界探测导致的静默数据丢失。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

论文研究不同图形处理器编程语言在不规则哈希分块截断符号距离场融合内核上的性能和正确性差异。

02
方法

作者用库达语言、锈语言和特里顿实现相同内核，并分别测量规则累加阶段与不规则探测插入阶段。

03
差异

分析把差异归因于特里顿固定上限探测和无掩码原子比较交换接口，以及锈语言原子读取的缓存行为，而非只比较最终速度比。

04
证据

规则阶段三者相差不大，锈语言在不规则阶段接近库达语言，特里顿慢一个数量级以上且可能静默丢失表面块。

摘要

UnionSparse: An Index-Efficient Sparsity Framework for Low-Bit Sparse LLM Inference on Edge

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Tianhao Jiang, Hang Gu, Teng Wang, Qianyu Cheng, ZhenDong Zheng, Cheng Tang et al.
high · 2026-08-10

Why it matters The paper makes sparse metadata and nonzero extraction explicit systems bottlenecks for low-bit decoding, giving edge-GPU inference engineers a kernel and encoding path beyond simply shrinking weights.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Low-bit quantization reduces weight payload but does not proportionally reduce sparse metadata, making index traffic and nonzero extraction costly in SpMM.

02
Method

UnionSparse combines Index-Efficient Bitmap Encoding with a Low-Bit Shared-Memory Parallel Decoding SpMM kernel.

03
Difference

The encoding amortizes metadata and matches sparse traversal to fragment assembly, while the kernel targets small-batch execution.

04
Evidence

At W4A4 and 30%–70% sparsity, the paper reports 1.43×–3.46× speedups over the listed sparse, CUTLASS, and cuBLAS Tensor Core baselines.

Abstract

Edge LLM inference combines sparsity and low-bit quantization to meet device memory, latency, and power limits. Yet quantization shrinks weight payloads without proportionally reducing sparse metadata, so index traffic and nonzero extraction become critical SpMM bottlenecks. We introduce the Payload-to-Metadata Ratio (PMR) and show that improving PMR raises effective compute intensity in decoding. We present UnionSparse, an index-efficient framework that combines Index-Efficient Bitmap Encoding (IE-BME) with a SpMM kernel using Low-Bit Shared-Memory Parallel Decoding (LSPD). IE-BME amortizes metadata and aligns sparse traversal with fragment assembly, while LSPD improves small-batch execution. Under W4A4 quantization and 30%--70% sparsity, UnionSparse outperforms FlashLLM and SpInfer by 2.30x and 1.43x, and CUTLASS and cuBLAS Tensor Core by 1.56x and 3.46x, respectively. These results establish payload-extraction efficiency as a first-order concern for low-bit sparse inference on edge GPUs. Source code is available at: https://github.com/Victor-Alen/UnionSparse.

Measuring and Reducing WebGPU Dispatch Overhead for LLM Inference

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Jędrzej Maczan
high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters This paper identifies operation-dispatch count, rather than kernel quality, as the bottleneck for batch-one WebGPU LLM inference. That gives browser and edge inference-engine developers a concrete target: reduce dispatches or amortize them across operations instead of optimizing kernels in isolation.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

WebGPU dispatch overhead in browser LLM inference is poorly measured, and single-operation tests mix dispatch cost with synchronization.

02
Method

The paper uses sequential dispatch measurements to separate per-dispatch cost from synchronization effects.

03
Difference

Unlike naive single-operation benchmarks, the method isolates dispatch count and examines its dependence on data type and batch size.

04
Evidence

The measurements report data-type-independent dispatch cost and show that dispatch overhead, rather than kernel quality, limits batch-one inference.

Abstract

Large Language Models are deployed to multiple types of environments, from internet browsers to edge devices, and WebGPU serves as a modern cross-platform standard. The engines for browser-based LLM inference have proliferated, yet the overhead of WebGPU per-operation dispatch remains poorly characterized. In this work, we introduce a sequential-dispatch measurement method and show that naive single-operation measurements overestimate per-dispatch cost by conflating dispatch with synchronization. Using our method, we measure the per-dispatch cost and show that it is independent of data type used. We show that the dispatch overhead, not kernel quality, is the bottleneck at batch size 1, and isolate the dispatch count as the cause. Therefore, we conclude that at batch size 1, the effective approach to LLM inference optimization in WebGPU is reducing dispatch count. Our findings point to dispatch amortization, in the inference engines and in the WebGPU specification, as a path to practical browser-based inference.

ReVolt: Power Delivery Network-Aware Voltage Droop Control for 2.5D PIM Chiplet Architectures

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicaccelerator / edge inference
Vibhanshu Sharma, Alish Kanani, Miao Sun, Janardhan Rao Doppa, Umit Y. Ogras, Partha Pratim Pande
medium · 2026-08-09

Why it matters This work brings power-delivery-network voltage droop into runtime control for 2.5D PIM chiplet systems, which matters to hardware and systems researchers deploying ML inference on multi-chiplet platforms. By tuning operation-unit size, it regulates chiplet current demand, avoids voltage violations without losing inference accuracy, and reports a 76x average EDP reduction over fixed and dynamic baselines.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Spatially and temporally varying chiplet current demand causes voltage droop in 2.5D PIM systems.

02
Method

ReVolt uses an LSTM-based PDN surrogate to predict per-chiplet voltage trajectories and adjusts operation-unit size at runtime.

03
Difference

It treats operation-unit size as an active control knob for chiplet current demand instead of relying on fixed or existing dynamic policies.

04
Evidence

Experiments report no voltage-droop violations, a 76x average EDP reduction over the stated baselines, and preserved ML inference accuracy.

Abstract

Processing-in-memory (PIM)-based 2.5D multi-chiplet platforms are enablers for machine learning (ML) workloads. However, their performance is affected by the power delivery network (PDN), where varying chiplet-level current demand induces spatially and temporally varying voltage droop. These droop events lead to voltage violations, degrades system performance, and impact inference accuracy for ML workloads. In this work, we propose ReVolt, a dynamic operation unit (OU)-based framework for mitigating voltage droop in PIM-based multi-chiplet systems. ReVolt leverages an LSTM-based PDN surrogate to predict per-chiplet supply voltage trajectories at runtime, enabling proactive adjustment of OU size to mitigate droop events. By treating OU size as a control knob, ReVolt regulates chiplet-level current demand while maintaining computational accuracy. This approach prevents voltage droop violations and improves energy-delay product (EDP) while preserving ML model inference accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that ReVolt prevents voltage droop violations while achieving an average 76x reduction in EDP compared to existing fixed and dynamic OU-based baselines, without compromising inference accuracy of ML models.

SpSYRK: Half the Work in Distributed Sparse Matrix Multiplication

Thomas McFarland, Julian Bellavita, Giulia Guidi
high · 2026-08-10

Why it matters The paper turns SYRK symmetry into less distributed sparse-matrix work rather than relying on a generic SpGEMM path. For similarity search, graph analytics, and genomics pipelines, it can replace an existing distributed SpGEMM call, expose triangular output directly to later stages, and reduce compute and memory use; on 32 Perlmutter nodes it reports up to a 2x speedup when local multiplication dominates.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Generic distributed sparse matrix multiplication performs redundant work for the symmetric rank-k update.

02
Method

The algorithms split off-diagonal output blocks across the upper and lower process-grid regions and compute only the lower triangle of each diagonal block.

03
Difference

A second variant changes the communication order so that the transpose of the input matrix does not need to be materialized.

04
Evidence

Experiments on 32 Perlmutter nodes show a 2x speedup over optimized Sparse SUMMA for multiplication-bound matrices, with the cost model explaining weaker gains on communication-bound inputs.

Abstract

The symmetric rank-$k$ update (SYRK), $\C = \A\A^\top$, computes the dot product between each pair of rows of $\A$, producing the Gram matrix $\C$. Its sparse variant underpins similarity search in machine learning, graph analytics, and genomics, including Jaccard similarity on datasets too large for a single node. Yet, despite the symmetry in its inputs and outputs, existing distributed sparse matrix multiplication algorithms, such as Sparse SUMMA, treat sparse SYRK as generic multiplication, leaving performance untapped. In this paper, we present distributed sparse SYRK approaches that leverage symmetry. The approach partitions the off-diagonal blocks of the output between the upper and lower triangular portions of the process grid and computes only the lower-triangular part of each diagonal block, reducing per-process communication and computation compared with state-of-the-art distributed SpGEMM. A second variant reorders communication to avoid materializing $\A^\top$. On 32 nodes of the Perlmutter supercomputer, the algorithm achieves a $2\times$ speedup over an optimized Sparse SUMMA on matrices where local multiplication dominates the runtime; the advantage narrows on communication-bound inputs, a dependence the cost model predicts from the arithmetic intensity. Our variant rectifies this and consistently achieves superior scaling at high process counts. The approach is a drop-in replacement for any application computing $\C = \A \A^\top$ via a distributed SpGEMM routine, and its triangular output can be consumed directly by subsequent operations, reducing both compute and memory footprint.

PSP: Low-Overhead Packet-Level Load Balancing for Stale-State and Bandwidth-Asymmetric Networks

Jiaqi Liu, Chunyang Zhang, Heng Pan, Yanbiao Li
high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters This paper targets a real AI-infrastructure bottleneck: microbursts and tail congestion in multipath data-center networks used by training and inference services. Its local probabilistic dispatching is intended to preserve packet-level balancing under stale telemetry and unequal link bandwidth, while avoiding the hardware cost of global ranking; the reported simulator results make it worth checking for network-stack and accelerator-cluster designers.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Flow-level hashing misses current link conditions, while existing packet-level balancers struggle with stale state, hardware cost, and heterogeneous links.

02
Method

PSP discretizes link conditions into bands and maps those states to per-path dispatch probabilities.

03
Difference

The algorithm replaces global sorting with local probability mapping to reduce herding and oscillation under stale information.

04
Evidence

A cycle-accurate simulator evaluates port scales, bandwidth-limited paths, and fixed-flow interference using loss rate, ninety-ninth-percentile buffer occupancy, and scalability.

Abstract

With the rapid growth of large language model training and generative artificial intelligence services, data center networks face severe micro-burst traffic and high concurrency. Traditional hash-based flow-level load balancing cannot sense link states, leading to hash collisions, hotspot congestion, and tail latency in multipath Clos networks. Existing packet-level schemes are constrained by stale state information, high hardware complexity, and poor adaptation to heterogeneous links. To address these issues, this paper proposes probabilistic state-proportional (PSP) dispatching, a packet-level load balancing algorithm. Using a Band-based discrete state representation, PSP replaces global sorting with local probability mapping, reducing hardware complexity while suppressing herding and oscillations caused by stale states. Experiments on a cycle-accurate simulator show that PSP is robust across port scales, bandwidth-limited paths, and fixed-flow interference. It outperforms join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) scheduling and Random in loss rate, 99th-percentile buffer occupancy, and scalability, while remaining competitive with Top-k at lower hardware cost. PSP provides an effective balance among performance, stability, and overhead for artificial intelligence data centers.

A Preliminary Study on Simultaneous Coscheduling for Discrete GPU vs. Fused GPU

Poorna Gunathilaka, Nabayan Chaudhury, Kirshanthan Sundararajah, Wu-chun Feng
medium · 2026-08-10

Why it matters This study gives systems researchers concrete evidence about how fused CPU-GPU memory affects coscheduling and programming effort: on GH200, more hybrid work splits become competitive, and managed memory works for several matrices without requiring all data movement to be manual. It is most useful for evaluating heterogeneous runtimes and accelerator platforms, although the evidence is preliminary and limited to sparse conjugate gradient.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper studies how workload partitioning and memory architecture affect CPU-GPU coscheduling efficiency.

02
Method

It runs sparse conjugate gradient on GH200 and H100 PCIe while comparing explicit copy, managed memory, and mapped memory.

03
Difference

It contrasts fused and discrete GPU platforms under the same coscheduling setting and examines the tradeoff from reducing manual data movement.

04
Evidence

The evaluation reports that GH200 makes several hybrid work divisions competitive and makes managed memory practical for several matrices.

Abstract

CPU-GPU coscheduling enables simultaneous execution of an application across both processing units, but its efficiency depends on workload partitioning and memory architecture. This preliminary study evaluates coscheduling on the NVIDIA GH200 Superchip compared to a discrete H100 PCIe platform. Using sparse conjugate gradient (CG) as a case study, we assess various work divisions across three memory-management paradigms: explicit copy, managed memory, and mapped memory. Our evaluation highlights the run time and programmability tradeoffs of reducing manual CPU-GPU data movement. The results show that compared with the H100 PCIe platform, GH200 makes several hybrid CPU-GPU work divisions competitive and makes managed memory practical for several matrices. These results suggest that integrated CPU-GPU platforms such as GH200 can improve both performance and programmability for coscheduled workloads.

SwiftQK: Fast and Communication-Efficient Tensor Parallelism for Query-Key Normalization

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicCUDA / kernel optimization
Gyudong Kim, Wonjun Han, Young Geun Kim
high · 2026-08-10

Why it matters This directly removes a communication bottleneck in tensor-parallel LLMs, with the clearest payoff for multi-GPU serving constrained by per-token latency; the paper reports a 29.5% average TPOT reduction over full-vector All-Gather and a further 14.3% reduction over an optimized scalar-aggregation baseline.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Tensor-parallel QK-Norm needs the full hidden vector to compute normalization factors, adding cross-GPU communication.

02
Method

The kernel exchanges only scalar normalization statistics and overlaps the remaining peer-to-peer reduction with independent element-wise work in a persistent kernel.

03
Difference

It replaces full-vector All-Gather with scalar-statistic exchange while hiding reduction work behind computation.

04
Evidence

The paper reports an 81.4–93.9% QK-Norm latency reduction and a 29.5% average end-to-end TPOT reduction.

Abstract

Query-Key Normalization (QK-Norm) improves the training stability and quality of modern Large Language Models (LLMs). However, under Tensor Parallelism (TP), layerwise QK-Norm introduces additional cross-GPU communication because the normalization factor depends on the full hidden vector. We present SwiftQK, a multi-GPU RMSNorm kernel that exchanges only scalar normalization statistics and overlaps the remaining Peer-to-Peer reduction with independent element-wise computation in a deadlock-safe persistent kernel. Evaluations on recent LLMs show that SwiftQK reduces QK-Norm latency by 81.4--93.9% relative to the standard TP QK-Norm using full-vector All-Gather. In end-to-end serving, SwiftQK reduces TPOT on average by 29.5% over the All-Gather-based baseline and by 14.3% over an optimized scalar-aggregation implementation.

What Irregularity Costs: CUDA C++, Rust, and Triton on a Hash-Blocked GPU Workload

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / GPU / Accelerator KernelsTopicCUDA / kernel optimization
Petr Korolev
high · 2026-08-08

Why it matters For GPU kernel and compiler engineers, this shows that language abstractions matter most on open-addressed tables, contended atomics, and data-dependent loops: they can change both throughput and correctness. The paper also ties Rust's slowdown to cache-coherent atomic loads and Triton's silent data loss to bounded probing.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

The paper examines performance and correctness differences among GPU languages on an irregular hash-blocked TSDF fusion workload.

02
Method

The authors implement the same kernel in CUDA C++, Rust via cuda-oxide, and Triton, then separate measurements for regular accumulation and irregular probing and insertion.

03
Difference

The analysis attributes the gaps to Triton's compile-time probe bound and unmasked atomic compare-exchange interface, plus Rust's cache behavior for scoped atomic loads.

04
Evidence

The regular stage is close across languages, Rust stays near CUDA on the irregular stage, Triton is over an order of magnitude slower, and bounded probing can silently drop blocks.

Abstract

GPU language comparisons are almost always run on tiled dense linear algebra, where every toolchain is good and the differences are small. We implement the same hash-blocked TSDF fusion kernel in CUDA C++, in Rust through NVIDIA's cuda-oxide, and in Triton, and measure it on a workload with the opposite character: an open-addressed hash table with compare-exchange insertion, data-dependent per-lane probe depth, and contended scatter. The result is a split. On the regular stage, which walks a truncation band and accumulates, all three languages land within a small factor of each other. On the irregular stage, which probes and inserts, Rust stays close to hand-written CUDA C++ while Triton is more than an order of magnitude slower. Language choice is nearly free on the work that is usually benchmarked and expensive on the work that is not. We attribute both gaps to specific things the languages cannot express, not to ratios. Triton's cost follows from a probe loop that must run to a compile-time bound and from tl.atomic_cas taking no mask, which forces a scratch structure with no counterpart in CUDA. Rust's cost was invisible in every instruction count: its kernel issues fewer instructions, fewer compare-exchanges and fewer registers at identical occupancy, yet was slower. Hardware counters located it in L1 residency. A GPU-scope atomic load must be coherent across SMs, no NVIDIA L1 is, so the type-correct way to read a shared location bypasses the cache on every access. Triton's bounded probe is also a correctness problem for fusion: at load factors an ordinary depth trajectory reaches, it silently discards blocks and the reconstruction loses patches of surface with nothing reported. We also report a defect found and fixed in cuda-oxide itself, now merged upstream: its scoped atomic load and store could not be called at all in the build mode that produces real kernels.

Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Serving EnginesTopicbatching / routing / latency
Kristian Schwethelm, Daniel Rueckert, Georgios Kaissis
high · 2026-08-10

Why it matters This work turns token-wise adaptive depth in looped language models into a deployable serving schedule: continuous batching at loop-iteration granularity and separate queues for boundary and loop stages deliver up to 99% of theoretical adaptive-depth speedup, 1.5–1.9× higher offline throughput, and 45–90% lower normalized latency under dynamic load.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Tokens exiting after different numbers of loop iterations cannot be handled by standard token-level batching because they must leave the batch during the forward pass.

02
Method

Continuous depth batching uses separate priority queues for loop steps and non-looped boundary stages, makes exit decisions one step ahead, and overlaps scheduling with GPU execution.

03
Difference

The scheduler operates on individual loop iterations rather than whole forward passes while accounting for embedding and language-model-head stages that run at different frequencies.

04
Evidence

On Ouro 1.4B and Huginn 3.5B, the system reaches up to 99% of theoretical adaptive-depth speedup and reports throughput and latency improvements under offline and dynamic serving workloads.

Abstract

A main promise of looped language models (LMs) is depth-adaptive inference. By iterating a block of shared layers a variable number of times, the model can use less compute for "easy" tokens and more for "hard" ones. However, this adaptivity breaks standard batching: tokens in the same batch now require a different number of loops, so there is no unified forward pass, making efficient inference difficult. Standard inference frameworks like vLLM schedule on the token level and cannot handle this because tokens need to be removed from the batch within the forward pass. Loop-level scheduling has been proposed as a solution, but never implemented end to end. The key challenge is that looped architectures also contain non-looped boundary stages (e.g., token embedding and LM head) that must be scheduled at different frequencies than the loop. We introduce continuous depth batching (CDB), which schedules at the granularity of individual loop iterations. CDB handles boundary stages and loop steps in separate priority queues, makes exit decisions one step ahead, and overlaps all scheduling work with GPU computation. On Ouro 1.4B and Huginn 3.5B, CDB can realize up to $99\%$ of the theoretical maximum speed-up from adaptive-depth, translating to $1.5$-$1.9\times$ higher offline throughput and $45$-$90\%$ lower normalized latency under dynamic serving load.

LLMVisor: A Real-Time Latency Attribution Model for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Serving EnginesTopicbatching / routing / latency
Shuowei Jin, Xueshen Liu, Jiaxin Shan, Le Xu, Tieying Zhang, Liguang Xie et al.
high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters Multi-tenant LLM serving needs request-level latency shares to enforce tenant-aware control and fractional engine sharing under co-batching. LLMVisor supplies this signal inside the scheduling loop using compute and memory-traffic features, with microsecond-scale overhead and substantially lower tail error than token-count attribution.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Co-batching hides how much latency each tenant or request contributes to a shared inference batch.

02
Method

The model uses features proportional to FLOPs and memory I/O traffic in a piecewise-linear roofline-guided form.

03
Difference

It decomposes batch latency into additive per-request shares instead of assigning cost from token counts alone.

04

Across Llama 3.1-8B and Qwen 2.5-14B/32B on A100 and H100 GPUs, it reports near-perfect R-squared and up to 2.5x, 3.3x, 3.5x, and 4.4x relative-error reductions at p90 and p99 for prefill and decode.

Abstract

As LLM inference shifts to multi-tenant GPU clusters, co-batching improves throughput but obscures per-tenant usage and limits control. Enabling fractional sharing of the inference engine requires a real-time, per-request attribution primitive that is accurate and light enough to run inside the scheduling loop. We present LLMVisor, a roofline-guided latency attribution model that captures the memory-bound and compute-bound phases via a concise piecewise-linear form over features proportional to FLOPs and memory I/O traffic. LLMVisor decomposes batch latency into additive, per-request shares and runs efficiently at microsecond scale. We evaluate LLMVisor across Llama 3.1-8B and Qwen 2.5-14B/32B on A100/H100 GPUs under varying tensor parallelism and workload mixes. Compared to a token-count baseline, LLMVisor attains near-perfect R-squared and reduces relative error by up to 2.5x and 3.3x at p90 and p99, respectively, for prefill, and by up to 3.5x and 4.4x for decode, despite batching variability and sequence divergence.

FlashBoot: Sub-Second Weight Loading for Large Models at Rack Scale

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Serving EnginesTopicLLM serving / inference engines
Issac Zhu, Hscos Zhang, Keith Jiang, Jack Li, Hugh Yin, Jason Zhao
high · 2026-08-09

Why it matters This targets a concrete serving-infrastructure bottleneck during elastic scale-out: a contiguous exportable tensor layout and communicator-free remote mapping reduce single-node loading from 20.1 seconds to 0.4 seconds and concurrent rack-scale loading from 87 seconds to 0.32 seconds, benefiting platforms that must bring many GPUs online quickly.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Weights are split into tens of thousands of per-tensor objects, while communicator setup and a serial GPU-to-GPU path constrain cross-node replication.

02
Method

The system uses a contiguous, exportable, inter-node-addressable memory layout with bulk CPU loading and remote GPU memory mapping.

03
Difference

Remote cloning avoids NCCL communicator setup and replaces fragmented transfers and serial replication with bulk or mapped access.

04
Evidence

On GB300 NVL72 with two MoE models, remote mapping takes about 10 milliseconds and sustains at least 700 GB/s per clone, while reported loading speedups reach 50x on one node and over 270x at rack scale.

Abstract

Flagship Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are growing fast along two axes at once: total parameter count and the number of experts. In elastic deployment scenarios, many GPUs across many nodes must become serving-ready quickly, and this growth makes weight loading a noticeable part of the latency budget. Even on NVIDIA's GB300 NVL72, today's state-of-the-art loaders leave most of that bandwidth unused. The losses are structural: (C1) weight memory is fragmented into tens of thousands of per-tensor objects, so transfers run far below link bandwidth; (C2) cross-node replication is gated by NCCL communicator setup, which costs 10-110 s before a single weight byte moves; and (C3) the existing cross-node GPU->GPU clone path is serial and scales poorly to concurrent multi-node bring-up. We present FlashBoot, a hardware-friendly, framework-workflow co-designed weight-loading subsystem built on SGLang. At its core is FabricArena, a contiguous, exportable and inter-node addressable tensor memory layout. On top of it, FlashLoad loads from CPU as a single bulk, zero-copy transfer, and FlashClone replicates a resident model from a remote GPU via a remote-mapping mechanism that removes NCCL setup. In experiments on NVL72 with DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, FlashClone maps remote weight memory in ~10 ms (versus 10-110 s for NCCL) and sustains >=700 GB/s per clone. Against the state of the art, FlashBoot accelerates single-node weight loading by up to 50x (from 20.1 s to 0.4 s) and concurrent rack-level weight loading by >270x (from 87 s to 0.32 s). Our code will be made publicly available.

OpRAG: A Resource-Deterministic Runtime for GPU-Backed Multi-Stage RAG Workflows

CategoryAreaInference Systems / Serving EnginesTopicagent serving systems
Arup Kumar Sarker, Mills Staylor, Aymen Alsaadi, Gregor von Laszewski, Shantenu Jha, Geoffrey Fox
high · 2026-08-08

Why it matters This targets a real serving bottleneck beyond LLM decoding: OpRAG makes RAG stages resource-aware and overlaps retrieval, embedding, and generation instead of leaving GPU-backed pipelines idle. The reported gains—about 16–21% end-to-end and 52–60% lower serving latency—make it relevant to researchers building agentic RAG runtimes, especially when kernel changes are not an option.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Multi-stage RAG workflows lose performance through serialization, fragmented scheduling, poor batching, and CPU–GPU pipeline stalls.

02
Method

The runtime represents embedding, retrieval, reasoning, memory, and upsert as operators lowered into communication-aware execution graphs with zero-copy transport, persistent workers, bounded queues, tokenizer prefetching, and overlapped execution.

03
Difference

Unlike flexible orchestration frameworks or general distributed task runtimes, it exposes RAG stages with resource-aware operators and deterministic execution semantics.

04
Evidence

Using Llama3-8B and Mistral-7B, the paper reports 16.16% and 15.66% gains over the nearest competitor and preserves 100% Recall@5.

Abstract

Agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems combine preprocessing, embedding, retrieval, memory access, context construction, generation, and vector-index updates. Although LLM decoding is GPU-bound, the surrounding orchestration layer can still limit end-to-end performance through serialization overhead, fragmented scheduling, inefficient batching, and CPU--GPU pipeline stalls. Existing frameworks provide flexible control flow, while distributed runtimes provide scalable task parallelism, but neither exposes RAG stages as resource-aware operators with deterministic execution semantics. We present OpRAG, a resource-deterministic distributed runtime for GPU-backed multi-stage RAG workflows. OpRAG models embedding, retrieval, reasoning, memory, and upsert as first-class operators and lowers them into communication-aware execution graphs. It combines an Arrow zero-copy data plane, persistent workers, bounded queues, CPU tokenizer prefetching, batched GPU embedding, and overlapped retrieval/generation execution to reduce non-model overhead around LLM inference. We evaluate OpRAG using Llama3-8B and Mistral-7B with FlashAttention~2, BF16 execution, and 32K RAG chunks. In end-to-end GPU pipeline experiments, OpRAG improves over the nearest competitor by 16.16% for Llama3-8B and 15.66% for Mistral-7B, and over RayScalableRAG by 20.57% and 20.71%, respectively. Against LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen, OpRAG is 17.77% and 17.48% faster than the best framework baseline. In Higress-style query serving, OpRAG reduces hybrid retrieval latency by 59.20--59.62% and generation-scenario latency by 52.48--53.55%, while preserving 100% Recall@5. These results show that optimizing the distributed orchestration layer can substantially improve GPU-backed multi-stage RAG without modifying the LLM decoding kernel.

Method brief
01
Problem

Hard SLO enforcement and ignorance of contention in shared resources can cause underutilization, degraded performance, and corrective rescheduling.

02
Method

The approach combines soft SLO limits with scheduling and rescheduling driven by real-time congestion signals for LLC and memory bandwidth.

03

Unlike strict-limit scheduling, it tolerates minor transient SLO violations and uses shared-resource conditions in placement and rescheduling decisions.

Workload scheduling in cloud environments often relies on simplistic assumptions about application resource needs and hardware utilization. Overlooking application-level performance objectives and hardware resource contention that leads to inefficient resource usage and degraded performance. This paper addresses two key limitations of current approaches. First, unnecessarily strict enforcement of service level objectives (SLOs) often leads to resource underutilization and poor energy efficiency. Second, lack of congestion awareness in shared resources such as last-level cache (LLC) and memory bandwidth. In this paper, we propose two complementary strategies to address these limitations: (i) integrating soft SLO limits that allow controlled overcommitment and tolerate minor, transient violations to improve cluster efficiency, and (ii) introducing resource-aware scheduling and rescheduling based on real-time congestion insights for shared resources such as last-level cache (LLC) and memory bandwidth. ARMOR: Accelerating RTL Simulation by Mitigating the Front-End Bottleneck Using Node Compression

CategoryAreaCompilers, Kernels, and Hardware / Compilers and RuntimeTopiccompiler / runtime
Jiaping Tang, Jianan Mu, Zhiteng Chao, Jingzhong Wen, Jing Ye, Huawei Li
medium · 2026-08-09

Why it matters This does not directly improve training or inference runtimes, but it can shorten hardware–software co-design and validation cycles for AI accelerators by speeding up RTL simulation. It targets a measured front-end problem—over half of pipeline stalls in the profiled simulators—and reports 1.6x speedup on CPU designs and 2.7x on AI accelerators.

Source signalsarXiv indexed
Method brief
01
Problem

Per-node lowering creates a code footprint that exceeds instruction-cache capacity and makes the CPU front end a major RTL-simulation bottleneck.

02
Method

The system identifies module-level isomorphic subgraphs, densely packs dependency-compatible nodes, and executes compressed nodes with unified bit-level parallelism.

03
Difference

It retains the optimization opportunities of an unrolled RTL graph while allowing one instruction sequence to serve multiple nodes.

04
Evidence

The paper reports 1.6x speedup on CPU designs and 2.7x on AI accelerators over state-of-the-art simulators.

Abstract

RTL simulation is indispensable in chip design. High-performance simulators typically lower each node in the RTL graph into an instruction sequence. Although this per-node lowering enables aggressive compiler optimizations, it dramatically increases the code footprint, severely exceeding instruction cache capacity and causing front-end bottlenecks. Our profiling reveals that over 50% of pipeline stalls are caused by the CPU front-end, becoming a key performance bottleneck in state-of-the-art RTL simulators. However, reaping the optimization benefits of fully unrolling the RTL graph while simultaneously reducing the code footprint to mitigate front-end bottlenecks remains highly challenging. In this paper, we propose ARMOR, an efficient RTL simulator designed to alleviate the front-end bottleneck through node compression. The key idea is to exploit the data parallelism exposed by the unrolling RTL graph and the insufficient bit-space utilization revealed by per-node lowering, leveraging bit-level data parallelism to compress multiple nodes simultaneously, so that a single instruction sequence can serve multiple nodes instead of one per node. To achieve profitable node compression, we first propose a module-aware isomorphic subgraph identification method that leverages structural isomorphism across module instances to systematically identify compression opportunities at the subgraph level. We then propose an alignment-aware dense packing strategy that groups nodes into packs according to dataflow dependencies while preserving data reuse, complemented by greedy merging strategies to enhance bit-space utilization. Finally, we implement a unified bit-level parallelism scheme to support bit-level parallel execution of compressed nodes. Experimental results show that ARMOR achieves 1.6x speedup on CPU designs and 2.7x speedup on AI accelerators compared to state-of-the-art simulators.

high · 2026-08-06

为什么值得看 它把智能体评测从短视频选择题推进到可持续交互、小时级记忆和工具调用场景，并显示持久多模态记忆与异步历史检索是处理真实流媒体任务的关键。

来源信号Hugging Face Daily Papers（社区点赞 👍 14）
代码
方法解读
01
问题

现有评测用短片和选择题衡量流式视频理解，无法检验长时记忆、实时感知和主动交互。

02
方法

作者构建包含二百四十三段长视频和三千六百四十六个开放问答的基准，并提出由前端工作器和后端工作器协同运行的双层架构。

03
差异

该架构将低延迟交互与主动监控同持久多模态记忆、历史回溯和外部搜索分开调度。

04
证据

论文称该系统在实时感知、历史回溯、主动交互和多模态工具利用四项能力上超过既有流式基线，并通过复用持久状态降低问答延迟。

摘要

论文发布了一个面向小时级交互式流式视频理解的基准，包含平均时长八十八点八分钟的二百四十三段完整视频，以及三千六百四十六个覆盖实时感知、历史回溯、主动交互和多模态工具利用的开放式问答。评测显示，仅保留近期画面、把历史观察转成文本或反复压缩视觉记忆，都难以同时保持长程理解与细粒度信息；论文提出的双层系统通过前端工作器处理低延迟任务、后端工作器异步建立持久多模态记忆并执行历史检索和外部搜索，据称在四项能力上超过既有基线且降低问答延迟。

Keyu He, Xuhui Zhou, Maarten Sap
high · 2026-08-10

为什么值得看 它用规则裁决的二十一种社交博弈和跨游戏等级分竞赛，替代昂贵而嘈杂的语言模型评审，并进一步提供无需更新权重的自博弈反思迁移流程，适合研究多智能体协作、谈判与角色适应能力。

来源信号arXiv 收录
方法解读
01
问题

多智能体社交能力缺乏客观真值，现有评估依赖昂贵、主观且有噪声的语言模型评审。

02
方法

社会健身房包含二十一种由规则决定胜负的社交游戏，并用等级分竞赛生成跨游戏排行榜；斯巴达让模型复盘轨迹和结果，提炼可迁移的对局手册并用于后续游戏。

03
差异

该方法把可验证的游戏结果与跨游戏竞争结合起来，并在不更新模型权重的情况下进行自我改进。

04
证据
